Primary CNS melanoma involving the spinal cord; melanocytic differentiation does not establish skin involvement.

Isolated spermatogenic failure causes abnormal sperm and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Primary skin lymphoma of mature T lymphocytes establishes cutaneous origin, hematologic neoplasia and the lymphoma mechanism axis.

Embryonal tumor originates in the kidney; lung and liver metastases and hypertension occur in fewer than 30%.
Congenital bilateral corneal tumors cause opacity and visual impairment; the definition explicitly excludes systemic abnormalities.
Necrotizing variant of phlegmonous bacterial gastritis causes gastric wall infection and gangrene.
Congenital duplication cyst of the esophagus; respiratory symptoms from compression do not establish common direct airway damage.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, most often gastrointestinal in origin. Pulmonary origin is a minority subtype; cardiac damage is not common across the umbrella.

Carney-complex phenotype includes defining endocrine tumors or overactivity, cutaneous pigmentation/myxomas and cardiac myxomas; type-specific phenotype data are limited.
